England's Best Campsites for Motorcycle Tourers

England's campsite scene has improved enormously in recent years. Gone are the days of muddy fields and communal shower blocks (well, mostly). Today's best sites offer firm pitches, hot showers, decent coffee, and locations that rival any hotel view. Here are our favourite English campsites for motorcycle tourers.

Lake District

Wasdale Head NT Campsite — At the head of England's deepest lake (Wastwater), surrounded by mountains. Basic but the setting is extraordinary. Book early for summer — this is one of the most popular sites in England.

Great Langdale NT Campsite — In the heart of the Langdale Valley, close to Hardknott and Wrynose Passes. Flat pitches on grass with mountain views. Stickle Ghyll tearoom and the Old Dungeon Ghyll pub are walking distance.

Baysbrown Farm, Chapel Stile — Small, quiet site in Great Langdale with excellent showers and a drying room (essential in the Lakes). Walk to the Wainwrights pub for dinner.

Yorkshire and the North

Hooks House Farm, Robin Hood's Bay — Clifftop site with views across the North Sea. Walk down the cliff path to the village for fish and chips. The coast road through the North York Moors is superb.

Dales Bike Centre, Reeth — Purpose-built for motorcyclists with camping, a cafe, and a workshop. In the heart of Swaledale. Community of like-minded riders.

Camping on a motorcycle tour transforms the experience. You wake to the view, hear the birds, and start riding fresh — no checkout, no fuss, no full English sending you to sleep.

Southern England

  • Tom's Field, Langton Matravers, Dorset — Walking distance to the Jurassic Coast, sea views from the tent
  • Eweleaze Farm, Osmington, Dorset — Seasonal clifftop camping (August only) with a private beach
  • Lundy Island — Campsite on this car-free island in the Bristol Channel, reached by boat from Bideford
  • Treyarnon Bay, Cornwall — YHA camping near a beautiful north Cornwall beach
  • Holmsley, New Forest — Forestry England site among ancient woodland, ponies wander through

Peak District and Midlands

  • North Lees, Stanage Edge — Dark Peak site beneath the famous gritstone climbing crag
  • Fieldhead, Edale — At the start of the Pennine Way, peaceful Kinder Scout setting
  • Clumber Park NT, Nottinghamshire — Mature woodland setting in the Dukeries

Motorcycle Camping Tips

When booking, ask about hard-standing pitches — soft ground and kickstands don't mix. Carry a flat piece of wood or a purpose-made kickstand pad to prevent your bike sinking. Most English campsites require booking in advance during summer and bank holidays. Expect to pay £10-25 per night for a motorcycle pitch. Many sites are cash-only in rural areas. faq.q: What should I ask about when booking an English campsite?
faq.a: Ask about hard-standing pitches, because soft ground and motorcycle kickstands do not mix. If only grass is available, carry a flat piece of wood or a purpose-made kickstand pad to stop your bike sinking. Also check whether the site takes card payments, as many rural campsites remain cash-only.

faq.q: How much does a motorcycle pitch cost in England?
faq.a: Expect to pay roughly 10 to 25 pounds per night for a motorcycle pitch at most English campsites. Prices rise at popular National Trust sites and during peak season. Booking in advance is essential during summer and bank holidays, when the best-located sites fill up quickly.

faq.q: Which campsites suit riders tackling the Lake District passes?
faq.a: Great Langdale National Trust campsite sits in the heart of the Langdale Valley, close to the Hardknott and Wrynose passes, with flat grass pitches and mountain views. Wasdale Head, at the head of England's deepest lake, is spectacular but basic, so book early for summer.

faq.q: Are there campsites designed specifically for motorcyclists?
faq.a: Yes. The Dales Bike Centre at Reeth in Swaledale is purpose-built for motorcyclists, offering camping alongside a cafe and a workshop, and it draws a community of like-minded riders. It makes an ideal base for exploring the Yorkshire Dales and its passes.

faq.q: Where can I camp near the English coast?
faq.a: Hooks House Farm at Robin Hood's Bay is a clifftop site with views across the North Sea, and you can walk down to the village for fish and chips. In the south, Tom's Field near the Jurassic Coast in Dorset offers sea views, while Treyarnon Bay gives YHA camping near a fine north Cornwall beach.
